news.title: Third quarter 2026 earnings released: EPS: ₹0.36 (vs ₹0.39 loss in 3Q 2025)
news.body: Third quarter 2026 results: EPS: ₹0.36 (up from ₹0.39 loss in 3Q 2025). Net income: ₹3.40m (up ₹5.19m from 3Q 2025). Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has increased by 65% per year but the company’s share price has only increased by 31% per year, which means it is significantly lagging earnings growth.

news.title: Thrive Future Habitats Limited announced that it expects to receive INR 219.999859 million in funding
news.body: Thrive Future Habitats Limited announced a private placement to issue 1,758,592 Equity Share at an issue price of INR 125.10 for the proceeds of INR 219,999,859.2 on January 22, 2026. Transaction involves participation of Rajendra Singh Pawar for 839,328 shares, Vijay Kumar Thadani for 839,328 shares and Neha Subash Idnany for 79,936 shares as an investors. Transaction is approved by board of directors and is subject to shareholder approval.

news.title: New major risk - Share price stability
news.body: The company's share price has been highly volatile over the past 3 months. It is more volatile than 90% of Indian stocks, typically moving 8.5% a week. This is considered a major risk. Share price volatility increases the risk of potential losses in the short-term as the stock tends to have larger drops in price more frequently than other stocks. It may also indicate the stock is highly sensitive to market conditions or economic conditions rather than being sensitive to its own business performance, which may also be inconsistent. Currently, the following risks have been identified for the company: Major Risks Less than 1 year of cash runway based on free cash flow trend (-₹24m free cash flow). news.title: Second quarter 2026 earnings released: ₹0.44 loss per share (vs ₹0.31 loss in 2Q 2025)
news.body: Second quarter 2026 results: ₹0.44 loss per share (further deteriorated from ₹0.31 loss in 2Q 2025). Revenue: ₹3.85m (up 70% from 2Q 2025). Net loss: ₹4.18m (loss widened 193% from 2Q 2025). Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has increased by 55% per year but the company’s share price has only increased by 16% per year, which means it is significantly lagging earnings growth.
